title: AI-Automated Morphological Feature Analysis of Bacterial Ultrastructures for CryoEM
content: Bacteria interact with the environment through dynamic subcellular structures. Rapidly tracking these structural features would be an advancement for clinical applications. Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) is a powerful high-resolution technique to image these dynamic bacterial features in biologically relevant hydrated conditions. Currently, bacterial structural feature determination in cryoEM images tends to be manually intensive [1]. AI-driven automated feature detection workflows need to be developed and implemented for cryoEM images to accelerate and enhance data processing efficiency. Methods for AI workflow implementation are on the horizon for biological EM-based techniques [2-6]. Here we present AI-based 2D image segmentation workflows to rapidly measure unprocessed cryoEM datasets. We utilize Pantoea sp. YR343 as a model for Gram-negative bacteria in cryoEM imaging to investigate its ultrastructural features [7]. Bacterial membranes (outer-to-inner membrane bilayer thickness and bilayer continuity), bacterial clustering propensity and flagella are selected as features of interest to observe dynamic structural changes. YOLO V8 (You Only Look Once) image segmentation models are fine-tuned using images of Pantoea sp. YR343 to detect features of interest. The tuned models are then deployed on large cryoEM bacterial datasets for rapid and dynamic detection of ultrastructural bacterial features [3]. We found that membrane bilayer continuity breaks, such as a ruptured or occluded membrane bilayers can be automatically identified. Additionally, variations of outer-to-inner bilayer thickness can be measured across the bacterial perimeter. Single bacterium and bacterial clusters can be separately identified. Flagella can also be individually detected, regardless of bacterial attachment. These bacterial structures now serve as targets for rapid automation in future research on the morphology of bacteria interfaced with antifouling and antimicrobial surfaces [8].
